comment: The IMO working list of major annual meteor showers, as data. Radiants are J2000 right ascension and declination at the peak; they drift a degree or so a day across a shower and that is far below what this panel reads to. Dates are the solar-longitude peaks expressed as a month and day, which move by at most a day between years. ZHR is the visual zenithal hourly rate under a perfect sky at the peak; it is the honest headline number and it is NOT what a radio operator receives, which is why the panel labels it as visual. Showers useful to meteor scatter are marked - the daytime ones are invisible and among the best on the air. Source: International Meteor Organization working list. Edit this file to add a shower; tests/test_meteors.py validates the schema.
source: International Meteor Organization working list of visual meteor showers

showers.name: Quadrantids
showers.note: Sharp maximum, only a few hours wide. Miss it and the shower is ordinary.

showers.name: Eta Aquariids
showers.note: Halley's dust. Strongly favours the southern hemisphere.

showers.name: Daytime Arietids
showers.note: The strongest daytime shower of the year and invisible from the ground. Radio operators have it to themselves.

showers.name: June Bootids
showers.note: Normally nothing; occasionally an outburst of a hundred an hour. Worth a look, never worth a plan.

showers.name: Perseids
showers.note: The reliable one, and the one every VHF operator schedules around.

showers.name: Southern Taurids
showers.note: Low rate, very long, and rich in fireballs — which is what makes a long burn.

showers.name: Draconids
showers.note: Storm years or nothing. Slow meteors, which ionise well when they come.

showers.name: Orionids
showers.note: Halley's dust again, from the other side of the orbit.

showers.name: Leonids
showers.note: The fastest of the majors. Storms roughly every 33 years; the last was 2001.

showers.name: Geminids
showers.note: The richest shower of the year, and the radiant is usefully high all night from mid-northern latitudes.

showers.name: Ursids
showers.note: Circumpolar radiant: up all night from the northern hemisphere, never up from the southern.
